definition: Salutary means producing a genuinely beneficial effect — often a shock or setback that does you good even though it stings at the time.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word salutary. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know salutary should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Losing the opening scrimmage 40–0 proved salutary: the team stopped coasting, rebuilt its defense, and never walked into another game overconfident.
Agreeable is far milder than salutary: an agreeable afternoon merely pleases while it lasts, while a salutary one leaves you measurably better off after it ends.
Transformative goes beyond salutary: a salutary setback improves your habits, while a transformative one rebuilds the whole enterprise into something new.
Beneficial means producing good results of any kind, pleasant or not; salutary narrows it — the benefit typically arrives through something unwelcome, a sting that turns out to be good for you.
Wholesome means good for health or character by its own nature — wholesome food, wholesome habits; salutary is judged by aftermath instead: even a defeat can be salutary if it leaves you better.
Corrective means designed to fix a fault; a corrective step is engineered on purpose, while a salutary one may be pure accident — the scare nobody planned that finally makes everyone careful.

The etiquette manual devoted its longest chapter to the salutation, and the young diplomat kept the book within arm's reach all posting long.
Salutary means producing a genuinely beneficial effect — often a shock or setback that does you good even though it stings at the time.
The editor's brutal notes turned out to be salutary — the young reporter shed her habits of padding and hedging, and the leaner stories she filed afterward won her the beat she had wanted for years.
Notice the arc: the experience was unpleasant, but its effect was health-giving, and that is the signature of salutary.
The word descends from Latin salus, 'health,' and it still grades experiences the way a doctor would — by whether the patient ends up better.
Salutary praises outcomes, not intentions, and it gravitates to unpleasant subjects: salutary lessons, salutary shocks, salutary defeats.
If the experience was enjoyable from the start, beneficial usually fits better — save salutary for the medicine that tasted terrible and worked.

In 2011 the seed bank failed its first outside audit, and the staff spent a furious week drafting rebuttals.
The auditors had found nothing dramatic — mislogged trays, a freezer door with a worn seal — but the report's tone stung, and the director refused to shake anyone's hand at the exit meeting.
A decade later she calls that audit the most salutary event in the institution's history.
The wounded pride turned into a rewired alarm system, duplicate logs, and a habit of inviting inspectors in early rather than dreading them.
When the region lost power for six days in 2019, the collection survived without losing a single tray — a fact the director reports, always, in the same breath as the audit.
